newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire troops switch to rebel side in Lubumbashi.
newsitem.headline: Zaire troops switch to rebel side in Lubumbashi.

text.p: Zairean army soldiers in Lubumbashi put on white headbands to symbolise that they had switched support to the rebel forces of Laurent Kabila, who began closing in on Zaire's second city on Monday.
"We've all changed sides. We're ready for the arrival of Kabila," said Sergeant Kafua Otamba of the 21st Brigade.

He was speaking at the Lido Barracks, one of many in Lubumbashi. Inside, dozens of soldiers were sporting white headbands, but it was not clear whether the army had gone over wholesale to the rebels, or what the elite presidential guard intended to do.
"We've suffered enough in Zaire over the last 30 years. We must get rid of (Zairean president) Mobutu (Sese Seko). We've had no pay and we have no food," Otamba said.

Cheering townspeople crowded around soldiers manning a roadblock outside the barracks. "We have suffered with these soldiers. We are very proud of them (deciding to change sides)," said Apollinaire Kasongo, a teacher.

Lubumbashi was braced for the arrival of rebel forces since the early morning when news reached the city that a large rebel force had taken the town of Kipushi on the Zambian border, less than 30 km (20 miles) away, and was advancing.
